Tâches de recherche en file

  • AE-DIGITAL-ACCESSIBILITY-DISCOVERY-001 — Découverte de sources — Non commencée

    Identify authoritative instruments and exact provisions for public websites; do not infer absence or legal effect.

Questions de recherche ouvertes

Ces questions sont des lacunes de recherche consignées, pas des conclusions juridiques.

  • Scope of public service sites and whether annex language establishes a binding legal obligation need legal review. (AE-01)
  • Whether separate built-in text-to-speech is mandatory or technology-neutral alternatives satisfy the requirement is not resolved. (AE-02)
  • It is unclear which user journeys, media types and service channels require each feature. (AE-03)
  • Whether the 2024 policy is a binding instrument and what enforcement follows a low compliance percentage or complaint is unresolved. (AE-04)
  • The Arabic policy page and the English policy PDF have not been compared, so authoritative-language status and translation provenance remain unresolved. (AE-05)
  • Scope is ministry-specific; do not generalize to all UAE organizations. (AE-MOE-ACCESSIBILITY-01)
  • Legacy-content exception has no documented sunset or objective decision criteria in this record. (AE-MOE-ACCESSIBILITY-02)
  • The use of an accessibility overlay does not establish WCAG conformance. (AE-MOE-ACCESSIBILITY-03)
  • The source does not establish the precise WCAG version/level. (AE-MOF-ACCESSIBILITY-01)
  • Agency pledge should not be conflated with national legal enforceability. (AE-MOF-ACCESSIBILITY-02)
  • Whether Articles 7 and 20 apply to government websites, apps and digital services, or only to the formats and services expressly listed, requires legal review. (AE-LAW29-01)
  • The implementing Cabinet decision and technical standards contemplated by Article 23 are not captured; their content and current status are unresolved. (AE-LAW29-02)
  • The relationship between this 2006 Law, Cabinet Resolution 43/2018 and the 2024 National Digital Accessibility Policy needs a consolidated reading. (AE-LAW29-03)
  • The official English translation and the Arabic text may differ; Arabic prevails and native legal review is outstanding. (AE-LAW29-04)
